rationale: Austin, San Diego, and Seattle stay the study markets. Each is one metro, the Inside Airbnb snapshot is from 2025, and bedrooms are almost complete. The other snapshots on disk were screened again for this round. Hawaii is several islands in one file. Asheville's bedrooms column is empty. Las Vegas, Fort Lauderdale, Nashville, and Washington have no nightly price on roughly 20–30% of rows. Boston, Denver, Dallas, Fort Worth, and New Orleans are missing a price on about 9–20% and are smaller. A fourth market with a large unpriced slice would not make the spatial test more honest, so the headline table is still three cities.

feature_set_why.size_and_room: How big the place is, and whether the guest gets the whole home or a room.
feature_set_why.plus_location: Where it sits: coordinates, distance to downtown, and distance to the airport.
feature_set_why.plus_census: The census tract around it: median income, median rent, median home value, and population density. A 2024 ACS 5-year join, not a listing's own price.
feature_set_why.plus_osm: What is nearby in OpenStreetMap: food, transit, parks, beaches, and attractions. Counts within 1 km and distance to the nearest, capped at 20 km.
feature_set_why.plus_structure: Building type, and two interactions: capacity priced differently for a room, and downtown distance priced differently for a house than a condo.
feature_set_why.osm_without_census: OpenStreetMap on top of location, with census left out, as a substitution check.
feature_set_why.target_smooth: Smoothed mean log price of the neighbourhood, and of neighbourhood by bedroom bin, fit on the training fold only. Unseen neighbourhoods fall back to the training mean.
feature_set_why.target_knn: Median log price of the 40 nearest other training listings. Under a 1 km buffer those neighbours are not next door.
feature_set_why.listing_quality: Amenities, reviews, and host fields from the current ad. Available for a listing that exists, not for a house that has never been listed.

protocol.selection_rule: Stage 1 keeps the simplest cumulative prefix within 1% of the best. A target encoding or listing-quality block is added only if it improves development MAE by at least 1%. Shallower trees win within 1%. LightGBM or CatBoost replaces XGBoost only if it is at least 2% better. Monotone constraints are kept when they are within 1%. An equal-weight blend of the two best libraries is kept only if it is at least 1% better. osm_without_census is reported and is not eligible.
